The *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text preserved within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Falling under the late sutta strata, the text belongs to the class of biographical narratives detailing the past meritorious deeds—specifically involving fruit offerings—and the eventual spiritual attainments of senior Buddhist monks [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive Pali-internal formulaic text reuse, with 149 shared passages across 63 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, nearly identical formulaic sequences (spanning segments 2.2–7.1) are shared with numerous other fruit-offering apadānas in the collection, notably a homonymous *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 470), as well as *Tālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 511), *Kadaliphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 389), *Bhallātadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 446), and *Udumbaraphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 385) [DharmaNexus].
